place.id: Kec. Bahorok, Kab. Langkat, Sumatera Utara
place.en: Bahorok District, Langkat Regency, North Sumatra

scientific.id: Angin Bahorok adalah angin jatuh yang hangat dan kering (efek foehn) di sisi timur Pegunungan Bukit Barisan, Sumatera Utara, yang bertiup di dataran Deli, Langkat, dan Serdang. Udara lembap yang melintasi pegunungan melepaskan hujan di sisi hadap angin dan kehilangan uap air; ketika menuruni sisi lee, yakni lereng timur, udara itu memanas secara adiabatik kering sehingga tiba di dataran sebagai angin yang lebih hangat dan lebih kering. Menurut Glossary of Meteorology (AMS), yang mengejanya “bohorok”, angin ini mulai bertiup pada bulan Mei dan tetap sering terjadi sampai September. Dampaknya pada perkebunan tembakau di dataran Deli membuat angin ini ditakuti. Pada hari-hari ketika angin ini bertiup, sisi hadap angin mendapat hujan lebih banyak daripada biasanya.
scientific.en: The Bahorok wind is a warm, dry downslope wind (the foehn effect) on the eastern side of the Bukit Barisan range in North Sumatra, blowing on the plains of Deli, Langkat and Serdang. Moist air crossing the range sheds its rain on the windward side and loses moisture; descending the lee side, here the eastern slopes, it warms at the dry adiabatic rate and arrives on the plains as a warmer, drier wind. According to the AMS Glossary of Meteorology, which spells it “bohorok”, it sets in during May and remains common until September. Its effect on the tobacco estates of the Deli plains made it feared. On days when it blows, the windward side gets more rain than normal.

sources.text: American Meteorological Society, Glossary of Meteorology: “Bohorok”

curator_notes: AMS ENTRY CONFIRMED from the text you pasted. The card paraphrases it (months, tobacco concern, windward-side rain, spelling 'bohorok') and cites it; the AMS wording is copyrighted and is deliberately not reproduced. It is a glossary entry, not research.

REMOVED from my first draft because the AMS entry does not support them: 'gusty' and 'damages crops'. The card now says only what AMS says: it is feared for its effect on the Deli tobacco plantations.
SPELLING: the AMS entry prints the plains as 'Deli, Langkat, and Lerdang'. The card says 'Serdang' (Deli Serdang), presumably the same place and a typo in the glossary. Please confirm.

UNRESOLVED, YOUR CALL: the AMS entry attributes the wind to the 'east monsoon' crossing the Barisan Mountains, while a European foehn-name list (EUMeTrain) reportedly says south-west monsoon. The card repeats neither. My reasoning, not a source: the Deli plains lie on the east, lee side of Bukit Barisan, so a foehn there needs air crossing the range from the west or south-west; air crossing from the east would put the foehn on the west side. So 'east monsoon' may be an old name for the dry-season monsoon and not a wind direction. If you want it in the card, tell me the wording (for example 'AMS attributes it to the east monsoon, a term that here denotes the dry season') and I will add it with the attribution.

Lead, unread: an Indonesian literature review on foehn winds (Jurnal Phydagogic, vol. 7 no. 1, 2024; ojs.unsulbar.ac.id/index.php/phy/article/view/3849) reportedly lists Bahorok under the Deli region. Its PDF could not be read here and the authors are not confirmed, so it is not cited.

Not found: no peer-reviewed study measuring Bahorok wind speed, temperature or crop damage turned up in my searches. If one exists it will help most; Indonesian journals and BMKG's North Sumatra office (BBMKG Wilayah I, Medan) are the places to ask.

Local knowledge: empty. Searches found nothing on the community's own account of this wind. Plantation-company records (for example the Deli Maatschappij) and Karo or Langkat Malay oral accounts are possible places, but this needs a named source; do not paraphrase from memory.
Local name: unknown. Is there a Karo, Langkat Malay or other name for this wind?
